ssh.lead: The hosts in your ~/.ssh/config: test the connection, open a terminal and edit without leaving Kabul. The file stays yours: every change shows the diff first and keeps a backup.
ssh.add.title: Add {alias}
ssh.noClient: The ssh client was not found. On Windows, turn on "OpenSSH Client" in Optional features; on Linux, install openssh-client.
ssh.search: Search by alias, address, user or key
ssh.noHosts: {file} has no host with an alias (only rules).
ssh.empty.title: {file} doesn't exist yet.
ssh.empty.lead: Add the first host: Kabul creates the file with mode 0600 (and the ~/.ssh folder with 0700).
ssh.conditional.hint: Comes from an Include inside a Host/Match block: it only applies when that block matches.
ssh.hint.host_key_unknown: this server was never seen from here. Open the terminal, check the fingerprint and accept it.
ssh.hint.host_key_changed: the server key changed since the last connection. Check with whoever runs it before removing the old known_hosts line.
ssh.hint.permission_denied: the server refused the offered keys. Check User, IdentityFile and the server's authorized_keys.
ssh.hint.timeout: nothing answered within 5 s. Check the address, port, VPN/Tailscale and firewall.
ssh.hint.dns: the HostName doesn't resolve. Check the name or use the IP.
ssh.hint.refused: the machine answered, but nothing listens on that port.
ssh.hint.unreachable: the network can't reach the host (VPN off?).
ssh.hint.passphrase: the key needs a passphrase and the test never asks. Load it into ssh-agent (ssh-add) or test from the terminal.
ssh.terminal.noWorkspace: Open a workspace to see the terminal, or run {cmd} in your terminal.
ssh.detail.siblings: The same block also applies to: {others}.
ssh.detail.forwardAgent: ForwardAgent is on: anyone who is root on that server can use your agent's keys while you're connected.
ssh.form.keyNone: None (ssh tries the defaults and the agent)
ssh.form.keyHint: Only the path goes into the config; Kabul never reads the private key.
ssh.edit.title: Edit {alias}
ssh.remove.title: Remove {alias}
ssh.remove.titleShared: Take {alias} out of the block (it stays for {others})
ssh.review.lead: Change to {file}. Before writing, Kabul keeps a copy (config.bak-kabul-<date>) and keeps mode 0600; the rest of the file doesn't change.
ssh.review.creates: {file} doesn't exist yet: it will be created with mode 0600.
ssh.rules.title: Rules
ssh.rules.lead: Wildcard and Match blocks apply to several hosts. Kabul shows them as they are and doesn't touch them; each host's final value shows under "Effective".
ssh.keygen.title: Generate SSH key
ssh.keygen.lead: Creates an ed25519 pair in ~/.ssh. Copy the .pub to the server (ssh-copy-id or the provider's dashboard).
ssh.keygen.name: File name
ssh.keygen.passphrase: No passphrase. To protect it with one, run ssh-keygen in a terminal: the passphrase never goes through Kabul.
ssh.warning.duplicate: Repeated alias: {detail} (ssh uses the first block)
ssh.mobile.title: SSH hosts
ssh.mobile.footer: The ~/.ssh/config of this computer. To edit, use the app on the computer.
